title: First-Line Supervisors of Helpers, Laborers, and Material Movers, Hand
description: Directly supervise and coordinate the activities of helpers, laborers, or material movers, hand.

tasks.text: Maintain a safe working environment by monitoring safety procedures and equipment.
Review work throughout the work process and at completion to ensure that it has been performed properly.

clusters.label: Resolving Conflicts and Negotiating with Others

tasks.text: Collaborate with workers and managers to solve work-related problems.
Resolve personnel problems, complaints, or formal grievances when possible, or refer them to higher-level supervisors for resolution.
Examine freight to determine loading sequences.
Provide assistance in balancing books, tracking, monitoring, or projecting a unit's budget needs, and in developing unit policies and procedures.
Schedule times of shipment and modes of transportation for materials.
Plan work schedules and assign duties to maintain adequate staff for effective performance of activities and response to fluctuating workloads.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Inform designated employees or departments of items loaded or problems encountered.
Conduct staff meetings to relay general information or to address specific topics, such as safety.
Inspect equipment for wear and for conformance to specifications.
Inspect job sites to determine the extent of maintenance or repairs needed.

clusters.label: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others

tasks.text: Participate in the hiring process by reviewing credentials, conducting interviews, or making hiring decisions or recommendations.
Recommend or initiate personnel actions, such as promotions, transfers, or disciplinary measures.
Prepare and maintain work records and reports of information such as employee time and wages, daily receipts, or inspection results.
Transmit and explain work orders to laborers.
Inventory supplies and requisition or purchase additional items, as necessary.
Estimate material, time, and staffing requirements for a given project, based on work orders, job specifications, and experience.
Counsel employees in work-related activities, personal growth, or career development.
Assess training needs of staff and arrange for or provide appropriate instruction.
Check specifications of materials loaded or unloaded against information contained in work orders.
Perform the same work duties as those supervised, or perform more difficult or skilled tasks or assist in their performance.
Quote prices to customers.
Evaluate employee performance and prepare performance appraisals.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Operations Monitoring
skills.def: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.

skills.name: Inventory management software
skills.def: Software to maintain the inventory of businesses including restaurants or retail shops. Examples: Inventory control software, Inventory management systems, Warehouse management system WMS.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Corel WordPerfect Office Suite, Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Enterprise resource planning ERP software
skills.def: Software to integrate, monitor, or analyze data from multiple business operations within a unified system. Examples: Sage ERP Accpac, SAP software.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.
